# RFC-0006: Controller pushes and signed commit provenance

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Will Eaton

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0006:C-SCOPE] Scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0006c-scope"></a>

Tasks change repositories they do not own and propose those changes as pull requests under the deployment's forge identity. Today a pack that wants this ships its own push logic: it holds a forge credential, builds commits, picks branches, and opens or updates pull requests. Every pack reimplements it, the credential reaches the run, and nothing records which run, model, or compute produced a commit except what the run printed.

This RFC moves pushing to the controller and makes every push carry a signed provenance statement:

- a task hands the controller a change and, optionally, agent-written text for the pull request; the controller builds the commit, pushes it with a forge credential it mints for that push, and opens or updates the pull request;
- the controller signs a statement binding the commit to the run and task that produced it and to the facts it recorded about that run; anyone holding the deployment's public key can check a statement without reaching the controller;
- public artifacts carry only an opaque reference to a statement. The statement names models, providers, images, and clusters, and stays with the controller, which discloses it to callers its API admits.

A statement attests origin. It does not say the commit is correct or safe; the check results it carries say which checks the engine ran and how they ended.

Commits stay reproducible: the same change on the same base produces the same commit SHA on every rerun, and nothing run-specific is written into a commit.


### [RFC-0006:C-TERMS] Terms (Informative) <a id="rfc-0006c-terms"></a>

- **Push**: a `draft-pr` write under [RFC-0001:C-OUTPUTS](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-outputs) that the controller performs: one commit on a branch of a target repository, and the pull request that proposes it.
- **Change**: the tree a task wants committed, delivered as a git bundle whose tip descends from a named base commit.
- **Statement**: an in-toto Statement v1 whose subject is one commit and whose predicate is defined in [RFC-0006:C-PREDICATE](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-predicate).
- **Envelope**: a DSSE envelope carrying one statement as its payload and one or more signatures.
- **Envelope digest**: the SHA-256 digest of the envelope's stored bytes, written `sha256:<hex>`.
- **Provenance reference**: the line `Crucible-Provenance: sha256:<hex>` naming one envelope digest.
- **Controller records**: what the controller itself resolved, performed, or stored for a run: its launch, the compiled workflow, the dispatch, the provider resolution, the pushes it made, and the run's evidence delivered under [RFC-0004:C-RUN-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-run-evidence).
- **Agent text**: anything an agent writes. It is payload, never a fact a statement vouches for.

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0006:C-PUSH-REQUEST] Tasks request pushes (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-push-request"></a>

A task proposes a change by asking the engine for a push, never by pushing or opening a pull request itself, and the engine sends the push request to the controller on the run's token. A sandboxed task MUST reach the engine's push only through the broker. This adds a grant to those [RFC-0004:C-RUN-EVIDENCE](../rfc/RFC-0004.md#rfc-0004c-run-evidence) lists: requesting pushes for the run the token was minted for. The push route MUST sit under `/api/evidence/runs/{run}/pushes`, so a deployment that exposes evidence routes to remote clusters exposes it too. The controller MUST NOT give a run the credential it pushes with or any credential minted from the same key.

A pack that uses controller pushes MUST declare, in its `draft-pr` output, a branch template, a commit message template, and pull request title and description templates, and MAY declare a path list. Templates MUST render only from the run's parameters; agent text enters only at the slots the title and description templates mark.

A push request MUST carry:

- the target repository and base branch, which MUST resolve from the pack's `draft-pr` declaration under [RFC-0001:C-OUTPUTS](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-outputs);
- the base commit SHA the change was made on;
- the change, as a git bundle;
- the task that produced it;
- optional agent text for the pull request title and description.

The controller MUST refuse a request whose target is outside the declaration, whose count is spent, whose bundle does not contain a commit descending from the base, or whose tree equals the base tree. Where the declaration lists paths, the controller MUST refuse a change that touches any other path. Each refusal MUST fail the request naming the reason, MUST be recorded on the run's ledger, and MUST NOT by itself end the run.

The reply MUST carry the commit SHA, the pull request URL, and the envelope digest of the push's statement, so later tasks in the run can act on the pull request.


### [RFC-0006:C-PUSH-COMMIT] The controller builds the commit (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-push-commit"></a>

The controller MUST create the pushed commit itself from the tip tree of the change. Only the tree comes from the task; the bundle's own commits, authors, dates, and messages MUST be discarded.

The commit MUST have the base commit as its only parent. Its author and committer MUST both be the deployment's forge identity, and its message MUST end with a `Signed-off-by` trailer for that identity. Its author and committer dates MUST be the base commit's committer date. Its message MUST be the pack's declared message template rendered with the run's parameters; agent text MUST NOT enter the commit message.

Given the same base, tree, template, and parameters, two pushes MUST produce the same commit SHA. A rerun that reproduces an earlier change MUST therefore push the same commit.


### [RFC-0006:C-PUSH-CREDENTIAL] Push credentials are minted per push (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-push-credential"></a>

For each push the controller MUST mint a forge credential scoped to the one target repository, with no permissions beyond writing contents and pull requests, and expiring no later than an hour after minting. The credential MUST be used only in the controller's process, MUST NOT be stored, logged, or sent to a run, and MUST be revoked when the push finishes where the forge supports revocation.

The key the controller mints from (for a forge app, its private key) MUST be held only by the controller.


### [RFC-0006:C-PUSH-BRANCH] Branches and pull requests (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-push-branch"></a>

The branch MUST be the pack's declared branch template rendered with the run's parameters, so reruns for the same target reuse the same branch.

When the branch does not exist, the controller MUST create it at the new commit. When its tip is the new commit, the push MUST NOT change it. When its tip is a commit whose author and committer are both the deployment's forge identity, the controller MUST move the branch to the new commit. Otherwise the controller MUST refuse the push: it never overwrites a commit someone else made.

When an open pull request from the branch to the base exists, the controller MUST update its description; otherwise it MUST open one as a draft. The title and description MUST be the pack's declared templates rendered with the run's parameters, with the agent text placed where the template says, after the controller strips any line that begins with `Crucible-Provenance:`. The controller MUST then add the provenance reference of [RFC-0006:C-PUBLIC-REFERENCE](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-public-reference).


### [RFC-0006:C-STATEMENT] Statement and envelope (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-statement"></a>

A statement MUST be an in-toto Statement v1 (`_type` `https://in-toto.io/Statement/v1`) with exactly one subject. The subject's `name` MUST be the repository's clone URL and its `digest` MUST hold the commit SHA under the key `gitCommit`. The `predicateType` MUST be `https://github.com/neuralmagic/crucible/provenance/commit/v1`.

A statement MUST be carried in a DSSE envelope with payload type `application/vnd.in-toto+json`. Each signature MUST carry a `keyid` naming a key in the key set of [RFC-0006:C-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-keys).

The controller MUST store an envelope as the exact bytes it signed and serves, and MUST compute the envelope digest over those bytes. It MUST NOT re-serialize a stored envelope, since a different serialization is a different digest.

One commit MAY have several statements, one per push that produced it. A rerun that pushes the same commit MUST get its own statement and MUST NOT reuse an earlier run's.


### [RFC-0006:C-PREDICATE] Provenance predicate (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-predicate"></a>

The predicate MUST record:

- `run`: the run id;
- `task`: the task id in the compiled workflow;
- `playbook`: the pack id and version, or the draft id and draft version, the run was launched from;
- `plan`: the digest of the compiled workflow and its parameter schema the run was launched with;
- `model` and `provider`: the model and provider the controller resolved for the task at dispatch;
- `sandbox_image`: the image the task's sandbox ran, by digest; a tag alone MUST NOT be recorded;
- `cluster`: the cluster the controller dispatched the run to;
- `base`: the base commit SHA;
- `pull_request`: the pull request URL;
- `checks`: one entry per check the engine ran for the task (a command or evaluate task whose exit status the run supervisor observed), with the check's name, its outcome, and the digest of its captured output;
- `signed_at`: the time the controller signed.

A field whose value the controller does not have MUST be absent; it MUST NOT be filled with a placeholder or a guess. A verifier reads an absent field as unknown.

The predicate MUST NOT carry secrets, credential names, prompts, agent text, or transcripts.


### [RFC-0006:C-FIELD-SOURCES] Every field comes from the controller (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-field-sources"></a>

Every predicate field MUST come from controller records. No field MUST come from agent text or from a task's report about itself. A signature over values the agent chose vouches for nothing.

The subject, repository, base, and pull request are what the controller pushed, not what the task reported. Check entries MUST come from the engine's record of tasks it ran, sent on the run's token, never from a task's report that a check passed.

The controller MUST produce exactly one statement per push it completes, including a push that changed nothing because the branch already held the commit. A push the controller refused MUST NOT get a statement. A commit pushed by any other means MUST NOT get a statement.


### [RFC-0006:C-KEYS] Signing keys (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-keys"></a>

The controller MUST sign with a private key it holds. The key MUST NOT be delivered to a run supervisor, a sandbox, or any pod the controller dispatches; signing MUST happen in the controller's process.

A key's id MUST be the SHA-256 digest of its public key bytes. The controller MUST serve its key set at `GET /api/provenance/keys` without authentication. Each entry MUST carry the key id, the algorithm, the public key, the time it became active, and, once set, the time it was retired or revoked. A deployment SHOULD also publish the key set somewhere that does not depend on the controller, so a statement can be checked when the controller is gone.

Rotation MUST add the new key before it signs anything and MUST mark the old key retired, not remove it. A statement signed by a retired key while it was active MUST keep verifying. A key marked revoked MUST fail verification for statements whose `signed_at` is at or after the revocation time; statements before it MUST be reported as signed by a revoked key, so the verifier can decide.

Keyless signing through a public Sigstore instance is out of scope for this version; see [RFC-0006:C-ALTERNATIVES](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-alternatives).


### [RFC-0006:C-STORAGE] Storage and lookup (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-storage"></a>

The controller MUST store every envelope it signs and MUST serve it by envelope digest at `GET /api/provenance/{digest}` and by subject at `GET /api/provenance/commits/{sha}`, which MUST return every envelope whose subject is that commit, newest first. Both routes MUST be open to any caller the human API admits and MUST refuse every other caller, including run and pod tokens.

A stored envelope MUST be immutable. The controller MUST NOT delete an envelope while a run that produced it is retained.

The run's page and its record MUST list the envelopes the run produced.


### [RFC-0006:C-PUBLIC-REFERENCE] Public reference (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-public-reference"></a>

The pull request description MUST carry the provenance reference of the push that last updated it, on a line of its own: `Crucible-Provenance: sha256:<hex>`. Earlier statements for the same commit stay retrievable by commit SHA under [RFC-0006:C-STORAGE](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-storage).

The reference MUST be the envelope digest, never the digest of the statement alone: the signature is part of what is hashed, so nobody without the private key can confirm a guess at the predicate's values from the reference.

A provenance reference MUST NOT be written into a commit message, trailer, or note. A commit's SHA MUST NOT depend on any statement.

Nothing public beyond the reference MAY name the run, model, provider, image, or cluster.


### [RFC-0006:C-VERIFY] Verification (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-verify"></a>

Verifying an envelope against a commit means, in order:

1. the SHA-256 digest of the envelope bytes equals the expected envelope digest, when one was given;
2. the payload type is `application/vnd.in-toto+json`;
3. at least one signature's key id is in the key set, and that key was active at the statement's `signed_at` and not revoked at or before it;
4. that signature verifies over the DSSE pre-authentication encoding of the payload type and payload;
5. the statement's `_type` and `predicateType` are those of [RFC-0006:C-STATEMENT](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-statement);
6. the subject's `gitCommit` equals the commit SHA, and its name equals the repository, when one was given.

A verification result MUST name the first step that failed.

The controller MUST serve verification at `POST /api/provenance/verify`, taking an envelope digest or a commit SHA and an optional repository, and returning one result per envelope.

`crux verify <digest|sha>` MUST run the same steps on the client: it fetches the envelopes from the controller, verifies each locally, and prints one result per envelope with the predicate's fields. It MUST accept a key set file in place of the controller's key route, and with one MUST NOT trust keys the controller serves. It MUST exit non-zero when any envelope fails.

## 3. Compatibility

### [RFC-0006:C-MIGRATION] Migration (Normative) <a id="rfc-0006c-migration"></a>

Until a pack moves to controller pushes it MAY keep pushing with its own logic and a forge credential of its own. Its commits get no statement, and the disclosure of [RFC-0001:C-CAPABILITY-DISCLOSURE](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-capability-disclosure) MUST list that credential.

The engine's publish-on-keep `draft-pr` MUST move to the controller push. The broker's approval `draft-pr` SHOULD move too, so every `draft-pr` write has one mediation point and one count.


---

## 4. Alternatives and open questions

### [RFC-0006:C-ALTERNATIVES] Alternatives considered (Informative) <a id="rfc-0006c-alternatives"></a>

**Pack-owned push logic.** It works, but every pack reimplements branch reuse, commit identity, sign-off, reproducible SHAs, and pull request updates, and each one holds a forge credential the run can read. A run that holds the credential can push anything the credential allows, so nothing it reports about a push can be signed as fact.

**Pushing from the run supervisor.** The engine already publishes kept candidates, so it could push for every task. It would still hold a write credential inside the run, and the facts a statement records would come from the run, not from the controller that launched it.

**Commit trailers with run ids.** A trailer is public, so it names internal runs to anyone reading the repository, and it is unsigned, so anyone can write one. It also changes the commit SHA on every rerun.

**Git notes.** Notes live under refs most hosting services neither display nor fetch by default, need push access to a separate ref, can be rewritten by anyone with that access, and are as public as the repository.

**Unsigned text in the pull request description.** Anyone who can edit the description can change it, and it publishes the same internal details a trailer does.

**SLSA build provenance as the predicate.** SLSA Provenance v1 describes a build turning source into an artifact. A commit an agent wrote is not a build output, and fitting run, model, and check results into its build definition would make SLSA-aware verifiers read claims about a build that never happened. A predicate type of its own says what it means; a later version can add SLSA statements for the images a run builds, where the model fits.

**Keyless signing with Sigstore.** Fulcio certificates and Rekor entries remove key custody, but the public Rekor log records every entry and the signing identity, which exposes each statement's existence, timing, and the deployment's identity. A private transparency log would avoid that and is a candidate for a later version once key custody under [RFC-0006:C-KEYS](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-keys) has run in practice.

**Signing the commit itself.** A commit signature proves which key pushed it, which is the forge identity, not which run produced it. It is part of the commit object, so a run-specific signature would change the SHA on every rerun.


### [RFC-0006:C-OPEN-QUESTIONS] Open questions (Informative) <a id="rfc-0006c-open-questions"></a>

- **Forge-signed commits.** A forge that signs commits it creates through its API marks them verified, but signs with its own key and the current time, so the same change no longer produces the same SHA. Whether a pack may choose a verified commit over a reproducible one.
- **More than one commit.** A push is one commit. Whether a pack needs a series, and how the controller would keep a series reproducible.
- **Ready pull requests.** Whether a pack may declare that its pushes open ready pull requests instead of drafts, and whether that needs its own output kind.
- **Other forges.** Forges without app credentials scoped per repository need another way to meet [RFC-0006:C-PUSH-CREDENTIAL](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-push-credential).
- **Signing key custody.** One key per controller deployment, or one per organization shared across deployments; held as a controller secret or in an external key manager that signs on request; who may rotate and revoke.
- **Storage and retention.** Whether envelopes live in the controller's database or its evidence store, and whether they must outlive the run's evidence, given a statement is only useful while the commit it names exists.
- **Disclosure.** Whether a deployment may publish a statement with some fields removed, and how a verifier tells a redacted statement from a forged one when the signature covers the full payload.
